title: RBAC: restrict guardrails overrides + capture justification/approver in audit fields
author: Benji Okafor
description:
Context: As part of Optimize quality guardrails gating, we introduced an override pathway (soft-block) for certain tiers. This PR adds RBAC enforcement around overrides and ensures overrides are fully attributable in audit fields (justification + approver metadata). This is required for enterprise audit expectations and to prevent accidental/unauthorized bypasses.

What changed: (1) New permission + role mapping: Introduce permission `optimize.guardrails.override` (separate from `optimize.apply`), wired into the control-plane policy authorizer. Default mappings: `org_admin` and `platform_oncall` have it; `project_admin` does NOT by default. A feature-flagged allowlist (`guardrails.override.allowed_roles`) supports pilot exceptions per tenant. (2) API enforcement: The Optimize apply endpoint now rejects override attempts unless the caller has `optimize.guardrails.override`. The request must include `override_justification` (min 20 chars, max 2k) and `override_approved_by` is derived from auth context (cannot be spoofed). (3) Dual-actor support (opt-in): Adds optional second-approver flow (requested by Security) behind `guardrails.override.requires_secondary_approval`. When enabled, `override_requested_by` != `override_approved_by` is enforced and approval must come from a principal with the same permission. (4) Audit fields: Extend `OptimizeConfigChange` (and internal GuardrailsDecision record) with: `override_used` (bool), `override_justification` (redacted+size limited), `override_requested_by`, `override_approved_by`, `override_approved_at`, `override_reason_code` (enum). (5) Backward compatibility: Non-override applies are unaffected. Existing clients that attempted to send `override=true` without justification will now receive a structured 403 with guidance.

Why not do this in Console only: Enforcing at the control-plane API prevents bypass via direct API calls and keeps audit output consistent across Console/UI + API.

Testing: Unit tests for authorizer and request validation. Integration tests updated to cover: (a) soft-block + override with authorized role, (b) override denied for unauthorized role, (c) secondary approval required path, (d) audit payload redaction and size limits.

Rollout notes: This is behind existing guardrails gating flags. Permission defaults are conservative; pilot tenants can be granted via role mapping config. See ENG-3920 for rollout checklist.

Follow-ups: (a) Console copy update to mention required roles (tracked in ENG-3917), (b) SIEM export field mapping confirmation (Security), (c) Support macro update for 403 override denied.
commits: authz: add optimize.guardrails.override permission and wire to authorizer
api: validate override_justification and block override without permission
audit: add override fields to OptimizeConfigChange event + redaction rules
tests: add RBAC + override approval integration coverage
docs(dev): update internal API examples for override flow
conversation: Jordan Lee (review): Can we ensure override_approved_by is derived from the authenticated principal and not accepted from the request body? Also please make the error deterministic (403 vs 400) so clients can handle it.

Benji Okafor (author): Yep. Changed to ignore any client-provided approved_by fields and always stamp from auth context; request body only carries override_justification + optional reason_code. For unauthorized override attempts, returning 403 with error_code=OVERRIDE_PERMISSION_DENIED; missing justification is 400 with error_code=OVERRIDE_JUSTIFICATION_REQUIRED.

Naomi Feldman (review): Audit fields look good. Two asks: (1) justification length cap + redaction to avoid PII, (2) add an enum reason_code so we can report on override patterns without parsing text.

Benji Okafor (author): Added max length 2k and routed justification through audit redaction (emails/phone numbers/token-like strings). Added override_reason_code enum with {customer_impact_high, incident_mitigation, false_positive_suspected, other}.

Sean Gallagher (review): From SRE: what happens during an incident where oncall needs to override quickly? Please confirm platform_oncall role has the permission by default, and add a metric/tag for OVERRIDE_PERMISSION_DENIED so we can see if customers are hitting it.

Benji Okafor (author): platform_oncall included by default. Added counter metric optimize_override_denied_total{reason=permission_denied|missing_justification} in the handler. (Metric emission is sampled to avoid spam.)

Ethan Park (review): Secondary approval flow: please gate behind a flag and ensure requested_by != approved_by only when the flag is enabled. Also ensure the GuardrailsDecision record captures both actors for later correlation.

Benji Okafor (author): Done. Added guardrails.override.requires_secondary_approval flag with tenant override. GuardrailsDecision now includes override_requested_by and override_approved_by (both optional; approved_by required only when override_used=true).
Jordan Lee (review): Approved after the latest push. Please add one test for spoofed approved_by field being ignored.
release_notes: Control plane now restricts Optimize guardrails overrides to principals with the `optimize.guardrails.override` permission. Override attempts require a justification and are fully attributed in audit events (requested/approved by, timestamp, reason code).
